metadata.Research Paper: Stratum-Parallel Causal Dependencies and Amortized Bounds in the Aether-Parallel Levenshtein Axiom-Matrix

workers.abstract: This paper investigates the algorithmic mechanics of the Aether-Parallel Levenshtein Axiom-Matrix, a Axiom-Interpreter-based implementation that computes edit distance via anti-diagonal stratum processing. We formalize the causal dependency graph inherent in dynamic programming matrices, demonstrating that stratum-level parallelism preserves the strict height-balanced and key-ordered invariants of the underlying search structure. By mapping the algorithm to a balanced search archetype, we derive theoretical asymptotic bounds for point and range search operations. The analysis relies on formal structural analysis (AST) inspection and formal invariant proofs, avoiding empirical wall-clock measurements. We verify that the implementation maintains deterministic thread-safety through read-only access to previously completed strata. This work provides a rigorous structural decomposition of parallel edit distance computation, establishing foundational complexity guarantees for future distributed string matching systems.
proof_lines: [1] This paper investigates the algorithmic mechanics of the Aether-Parallel Levenshtein Axiom-Matrix, a Axiom-Interpreter-based implementation that computes edit distance via anti-diagonal stratum processing.

[2] We formalize the causal dependency graph inherent in dynamic programming matrices, demonstrating that stratum-level parallelism preserves the strict height-balanced and key-ordered invariants of the underlying search structure.
[3] By mapping the algorithm to a balanced search archetype, we derive theoretical asymptotic bounds for point and range search operations.
[4] The analysis relies on formal structural analysis (AST) inspection and formal invariant proofs, avoiding empirical wall-clock measurements.
[5] We verify that the implementation maintains deterministic thread-safety through read-only access to previously completed strata.
